Sample And Hold.description: Samples input values when corresponding gate is 1. In non-edge mode, continuously samples while the gate is high. In edge mode, values are sampled on the rising edge; Edge High and Edge Low choose which gate transitions send the held values through the outputs.

Save Vectors To File.description:
Writes several float vectors to a CSV file, with one input vector per file row.

**Controls**

**[ Choose Folder]** Opens a folder chooser to select the destination directory.

**[ Filename]** Name of the file to write, including its extension.

**[ Save To File]** Writes the current row inputs. An existing file at the same destination is overwritten.

**Row inputs**

**[ row_0]** Float vector written as CSV row 1. Values are separated by commas.

**[ row_1]** Float vector written as CSV row 2. Values are separated by commas.

**[ row_2]** Float vector written as CSV row 3. Values are separated by commas.

**[ row_3]** Float vector written as CSV row 4. Values are separated by commas.

**[ row_4]** Float vector written as CSV row 5. Values are separated by commas.

**[ row_n]** Additional float-vector row created by increasing Num Rows. n is the zero-based row index.

**Output**

**[ Folder Path]** Path of the directory selected with Choose Folder; reports the selection rather than selecting a folder itself.

**Inspector**

**[ Num Rows]** Number of row inputs. Increasing it adds rows; decreasing it removes rows from the end.

**Notes**

Choose a folder and provide a non-empty filename before saving. Row lengths can differ. Saving happens only when Save To File fires, not on every input edit.

Sc RecBuf.description: Records SuperCollider audio into a buffer and saves recordings to a selected folder.

Scala Tuning.description: Converts MIDI notes to microtonal frequencies using Scala (.scl) tuning files or custom ratios. Supports both direct (scale degree based) and modular (12-TET based) mapping modes.

Schoenberg Matrix.description: Twelve-tone serial matrix generator with experimental features. Standard dodecaphonic technique with optional chaos/generative controls.

Segment Length.description: calculates the length of segments and their midpoints

Segments Maker.description: Builds segments between selected XY vertices or all point pairs.

Sequential Analyzer.description: Analyzes an input sequence with threshold, step and reset controls, outputting values, pulses and counts.

Set Pan/Tilt/Roll.description: Sets the ASTRES viewing orientation from pan, tilt and roll inputs.

Shader.description: Edits, previews, loads and saves GLSL texture effects with optional AI assistance.

Shape Feather.description: Calculates feathering values along an XY shape.

Shape Length.description: Calculates the length of an XY shape.

Shape Transform.description: Translates, scales, rotates and replicates XY shapes with optional output clamping.

Shell.description: Runs the configured shell command when Exec is triggered.

Shuffle.description: The Shuffle node rearranges elements within an input vector based on a control signal.

Sigmoid Curve.description: Edits multiple sigmoid curves and evaluates their values at the input phase.

Signes Manual Drawer.description:
Edits a grid of eight cell states and converts it to angle and state-mask vectors. Stores 32 independent drawing slots.

**Grid and display controls**

**[ Grid X]** Column counts. One value applies to every row; a vector sets each row separately, repeating its last value for later rows.

**[ Grid Y]** Number of grid rows.

**[ w]** Width of the entire grid in canvas units.

**[ h]** Height of each grid row in canvas units.

**[ Slot]** Drawing slot to display and output, indexed from 0 to 31.

**[ Reset Slot]** Clears every cell in the current slot to state 0.

**[ Reset All]** Clears every cell in all drawing slots to state 0.

**[ Open]** Opens a saved JSON drawing collection.

**[ Save]** Saves the drawing collection as JSON.

**Outputs**

**[ Curr.File]** Filename of the current external drawing collection.

**[ Angle out]** One angle per cell in turns: state times 0.125, from 0 to 0.875.

**[ O1]** 1 where a cell is state 1 (blue), otherwise 0.

**[ O2]** 1 where a cell is state 2 (green), otherwise 0.

**[ O3]** 1 where a cell is state 3 (yellow), otherwise 0.

**[ O4]** 1 where a cell is state 4 (orange), otherwise 0.

**[ O5]** 1 where a cell is state 5 (red), otherwise 0.

**[ O6]** 1 where a cell is state 6 (magenta), otherwise 0.

**[ O7]** 1 where a cell is state 7 (cyan), otherwise 0.

**[ O8]** 1 where a cell is state 0 (empty), otherwise 0.

**Notes**

Click a cell to advance its state; Shift-click moves backward. Drag paints other cells with the state selected by the first click. Outputs follow reading order, left to right and then top to bottom. Grid resizing preserves overlapping cells in every slot.

Skull Illusion.description:
Converts a texture into a grid of complementary half-hexagon tiles, producing the Skull Illusion pattern.

**Input**

**[ Input Texture]** Source texture used to choose the tile pattern from sampled brightness.

**Controls**

**[ Threshold]** Brightness cutoff used to select the two tile states.

**[ Divisions]** Number of grid cells along each axis. Higher values give smaller, more detailed tiles.

**[ Draw Mode]** 0 uses CPU vectorial shapes; 1 uses CPU lineal shapes; 2 uses the GPU shader.

**[ Invert]** Reverses the brightness classification used for the pattern.

**[ Dark Color]** Color used for the dark parts of the pattern.

**[ Light Color]** Color used for the light parts and background of the pattern.

**[ Out Width]** Output texture width in pixels.

**[ Out Height]** Output texture height in pixels.

**[ Save]** Exports CPU vectorial and lineal versions as SVG and the GPU version as PNG into a timestamped data/skullIllusionRenders folder.

**Output**

**[ Output Texture]** Rendered pattern texture at the selected output dimensions.

**Notes**

GPU mode renders every update to follow live texture contents. CPU modes recompute when their input or controls report changes. Save exports all three versions and then restores the selected draw mode.

Slider.description: A slider with transparent background, bindable to float portals.

Slope.description: Calculates slopes from input X and Y vectors.

Slot Easer.description: Interpolates between configurable value slots using phase and curve shaping.

Smoother.description: Uses moving average to smooth the signal with custom laggy tension implementation

Solo Sequencer.description: A sequencer node that outputs a number based on weighted probabilities from eight input vectors. The 'step' input determines the index for reading values from each input vector. 'Hold Mode' allows the output to update only when there are changes in the input vectors' values.

Solo Sequencer GUI.description:
Weighted solo sequencer with editable probability tracks.
Keeps the soloSequencer behavior, but tracks are created inside a custom GUI instead of fixed vector inputs.

Solo Step Sequencer.description: A sequencer node that outputs a number based on weighted probabilities from multiple tracks. Each track has its own multislider for entering values. 'Hold Mode' allows the output to update only when there are changes in the steps' values.

Spectrogram Shift.description: Scrolls incoming spectrum data into a history buffer with configurable width and speed.

Sphere Renderer.description:
Creates a textured sphere for rendering in the Equirectangular Pipeline.

**Geometry**

**[ Sph.Radius]** Sphere radius in scene units.

**[ Sph.Resolution]** Sphere tessellation resolution. Higher values produce more vertices and a smoother surface.

**Texture and transform**

**[ Tex.In]** Optional surface texture. Connect Mesh Out to an Equirectangular Pipeline mesh input to render it.

**[ PosX]** Mesh translation along the scene X axis.

**[ PosY]** Mesh translation along the scene Y axis.

**[ PosZ]** Mesh translation along the scene Z axis.

**[ ScaleX]** Scale multiplier along the mesh X axis.

**[ ScaleY]** Scale multiplier along the mesh Y axis.

**[ ScaleZ]** Scale multiplier along the mesh Z axis.

**[ RotX]** Rotation about the X axis, in degrees.

**[ RotY]** Rotation about the Y axis, in degrees.

**[ RotZ]** Rotation about the Z axis, in degrees.

**[ FlipX]** Mirrors texture coordinates horizontally. Does not mirror the geometry.

**[ FlipY]** Mirrors texture coordinates vertically. Does not mirror the geometry.

**Output**

**[ Mesh Out]** Reference to this mesh for an Equirectangular Pipeline Mesh input. This is a mesh object, not an image texture.

**Notes**

Geometry and transforms use scene units rather than normalized 0-1 coordinates. This node supplies mesh data; the connected pipeline performs rendering.

Split MinMax.description: Lets values pass if they are between the specified min and max values.

Split Resize.description: Splits the input vector into N equal regions and resizes each region independently using interpolation.

Split Route.description: Routes values from the input to one of the two outputs based on comparison with a threshold.

Spliter x2.description: Copies a Playmodes video frame to two outputs.

Star Data Extractor.description: Looks up catalog attributes for HIP identifiers, including magnitude, parallax, spectral type and constellation.

Star In Region.description: Finds catalog stars inside an XY region and outputs their identifiers, magnitudes and positions.

Star2Laser.description: Projects HIP star identifiers into laser XY coordinates with optional frustum clipping.

StarFormation.description: Sorts and arranges input star points around a configurable center.

StarWatcher Control.description: Sends pan, tilt, speed, acceleration and laser intensity commands to a StarWatcher controller.

StarWatcher Debug.description: Queries status, position, calibration and errors from a StarWatcher controller over OSC.

Stars Catalog.description: Browses and selects entries from the star catalog.

Stars Info.description: Looks up star coordinates, magnitude and distance from the viewing frustum for HIP identifiers.

Statistics.description: Calculates weighted mean, variance and mean variation over input history.

Step Sequencer.description: Outputs the configured step value at an incoming index.

Step Value Track.description: Edits and plays a timeline step-value clip with a configurable output range.

String Box.description: Displays text in a resizable box with adjustable font size.

String Comparator.description: Compares two string inputs. Outputs 1 when strings are equal, 0 when different.

String Switch.description: Switches between multiple string inputs based on switch parameter. Number of inputs is configurable in inspector.

String Vector.description: Splits a comma-separated string into a vector of strings.

String to Float.description: Converts a string of numbers into a vector of floats using a custom separator.

StrobeLight Controller.description: Maps color, fader, strobe and effect controls to lighting fixture channel data.

SubDimension Combinator.description: Combines an original vector with a sub-dimension vector.

SubTexture.description: Extracts a rectangular region from an input texture.

Switcher.description: Selects between two Playmodes video frame inputs.

Switcher Float.description: Select one of the inputs to send to the output (with linear interpolation)

Sym.Structures.description: Finds symmetric star structures around an angle with distance and magnitude constraints.

SynScan Ctrl.description: Controls a SynScan mount over the network, including go-to, slewing and position queries.

Table.description: Loads, edits and saves a numeric table with selectable row and column outputs.

Table Row Id.description: Loads and edits a numeric table with row identifiers, row and column selection, filtering and file saving.

Tex To VideoFrame.description: Converts an OpenGL texture into a Playmodes video frame.

Text Box.description:
Displays an editable text panel inside the node, with automatic wrapping in display mode.

**Control**

**[ Edit]** Enables multiline text editing in the panel. Turn it off to show the wrapped display view.

**Inspector**

**[ Text]** Text to display or edit. Changes made in the panel are written back here.

**[ w]** Panel width in canvas units. Also adjustable by dragging the bottom-right resize handle.

**[ h]** Panel height in canvas units. Also adjustable by dragging the bottom-right resize handle.

**[ Backgr.Color]** Panel background color, including alpha.

**[ Text.Color]** Displayed text color, including alpha.

**[ Font Size]** Text size at normal canvas zoom; scales with the canvas.

**Notes**

Display text is clipped to the panel bounds. The panel stores plain text; the bold-description syntax belongs to the help views and is not interpreted by this node.

Text Reader.description: Reads text from a file specified by path or selected through a file dialog. Line breaks are replaced with spaces.

Texture Blender.description:
Composites textures using the matrices in T. In.
Show opens a 3D preview with an independent navigation camera and optional texture display.

Texture Channels.description: Separates a texture into red, green, blue and alpha channels.

Texture Composer.description: Composes an input texture using anchor, position, rotation and scale transforms.

Texture Composer Simple.description: Places multiple textures in an output canvas using per-layer XY position and opacity.

Texture Display.description:
Displays a texture from a portal with a resizable area.
Accepts a direct ofTexture* input (top-left pin) which overrides the portal selection.

Texture Easer.description: Crossfades between texture changes using triggered snapshots, input phase and easing curves.

Texture Feedback Delay.description:
A one-iteration texture delay for patchable feedback. Connect an initial image to Seed, send Output through any processing nodes, and connect the final result to Return. The returned image is published on the next update, never during its Return callback.

Run: advance once per application update. Turn off to hold the displayed frame.
Step: while paused, process the displayed frame once; press again to show its returned result.
Reset: discard the loop and seed again on the next update.
Iteration: number of returned images published since reset.
Inputs must be GL_TEXTURE_2D; use Texture Resizer for other texture targets.

Texture Flip.description: Flips the input texture in the horizontal or vertical axis based on the toggles.

Texture Info.description: Reports the dimensions and format of an input texture.

Texture Reader.description: Reads texture pixels into channel vectors and a combined output vector.

Texture Receiver.description: Receives a shared texture from a selected server.

Texture Recorder.description: Records input texture frames with phase, alpha and video creation controls.

Texture Recorder FFmpeg.description: Records texture inputs to video through FFmpeg with frame rate, alpha and optional audio controls.

Texture Resizer.description: Resizes an input texture to a chosen width and height with selectable interpolation.

Texture Resizer Fast.description: Resizes a texture using a fast rendering path with selectable interpolation.

Texture Sender.description: Publishes an input texture to a texture sharing server.

Texture Snapshot.description: Captures the input texture when Snap is triggered and holds it at the output.

Texture Unifier.description: Combines texture inputs into a unified layout with spacing, position and opacity controls.

Texture Unifier Forms.description: Combines Forms textures with spacing, position and opacity controls.

Texture Unit Monitor.description: Reports active texture units, usage and warnings, with scanning and diagnostic controls.

Threshold.description: Detects threshold crossings and outputs state, changes and frame events.

Time Passed.description:
Measures the elapsed time between changes to an input vector.

**Inputs and controls**

**[ Input]** A vector change marks a new event; its values do not affect the timing calculation.

**[ Verbose]** Logs each input event, its values and the elapsed interval to the console.

**Output**

**[ Output]** Seconds since the preceding input event. The console shows the interval in milliseconds.

**Notes**

Only intervals after the first event have a defined previous-event reference. Uses application elapsed time rather than Oceanode transport time.

Toggle.description: A resizable toggle switch that connects to a boolean portal.

Track Scheduler.description: Schedules a named track in the PPQ timeline.

Transformations.description: Applies bypass, inversion, reciprocal, negation, absolute value, floor, round or ceiling to each input element.

Transport Quantizer.description: Defers input events to the selected beat transport grid.

Trigger.description: Generates probabilistic triggers from phase, change, event and gate inputs with optional transport synchronization.

Trigonometry.description: Performs various trigonometric operations on each element of the input vector.

Trim Group Paths.description: Groups multiple input paths and trims each group sequentially. Click 'Focus' on a group to select paths by clicking on them in the visual preview. Paths can belong to multiple groups. Start/End/Opacity vectors control each group independently. Endpoint Dots adds a dot at each segment endpoint.

Trim Path.description:
Trims each straight segment of input polylines between normalized start and end positions.

**Inputs**

**[ In.X]** X coordinates of the paths. A -1 separates paths.

**[ In.Y]** Y coordinates of the paths. A -1 separates paths.

**[ Start]** Start fraction along each segment: 0 is its first vertex and 1 its second vertex.

**[ End]** End fraction along each segment: 0 is its first vertex and 1 its second vertex.

**[ Keep Order]** When enabled, Start greater than End removes the segment. When disabled, the smaller fraction is used as the start.

**Outputs**

**[ Out.X]** X coordinates of retained segment endpoints, with -1 separators.

**[ Out.Y]** Y coordinates of retained segment endpoints, with -1 separators.

**[ Completeness]** Retained fraction for each original segment; 0 means removed.

**[ FullSegment.X]** Fixed-slot X output: start, end, -1 for each original segment. Removed segments use 0, 0, -1.

**[ FullSegment.Y]** Fixed-slot Y output: start, end, -1 for each original segment. Removed segments use 0, 0, -1.

**Notes**

Start and End must both contain either one value, one value per polyline, or one value per original segment. These fractions apply within each segment, not to the total arc length of a path. Recalculates on In.X changes; other edits take effect on the next In.X update.

Trim Path Sequential.description: Sequential version of Trim Path. When Sequential is false, behaves like regular Trim Path. When Sequential is true, trimming progresses through segments sequentially from first to last, creating animated path reveal effects. Start and End parameters control the overall progress through all segments.

USB Keyboard.description:
Captures USB HID key events from the configured MagicForce MF34 keyboard on macOS.

**Outputs**

**[ Key Code]** USB HID usage code for the latest key press. Releases are ignored, so it retains its last value between presses.

**[ Connected]** Read-only indication that the matching device is connected.

**[ Device Name]** Read-only product name reported by the connected device.

**Notes**

Requires macOS Input Monitoring permission. Device matching uses the vendor and product IDs compiled into this node; other keyboards require changing those IDs. Key codes are HID usages, not typed characters.

Unrepeated Random.description: This module generates random numbers in a given range. It has a sequential mode where it ensures all numbers within the range are generated before repeating. Trigger reacts to rising edges; EvenTrig is a legacy-named event input that reacts to every received update.

VV Indexed Sampler.description: Samples a vector of vectors using separate vector and element indices.

Value.description: A numeric input field that connects to a float portal.

Value Easer.description: Interpolates input values using phase and curve shaping, with circular path options.

Value Index.description: Searches for specific values within an input vector and returns all their indices. Accepts multiple search values and outputs corresponding indices in a flat vector, using -1 as a separator between different search values. Returns an empty vector if no values are found.

Value Mod.description: Applies random variation, scale, offset, powers, quantization, fading and inversion to input values.

Value Remover.description:
Filters a float vector by removing values close to a chosen target.

**Input and controls**

**[ Input]** Vector to filter. The order of retained elements is preserved.

**[ Value]** Target value to remove.

**[ Thresh.]** Inclusive tolerance around Value. Elements with absolute difference less than or equal to this value are removed.

**Output**

**[ Output]** Remaining values, with removed elements compacted out of the vector.

**Notes**

Recalculates when Input or Value changes. A change to Thresh. takes effect on the next such recalculation.

Values Changed.description:
Detects changes in the input vector in three modes:

0) Index-by-Index:
   - Compares old vs new index-by-index.
   - Reports changed or newly added/removed indices explicitly.
   - Reordering => changes.

1) Set-Based (Original):
   - Uses a set of values to detect if a value completely
     appears or disappears.
   - Duplicates collapse; partial additions/removals aren't reported.
   - Reordering is ignored.

2) Frequency-Based:
   - Compares the count of each value in old vs new.
   - Reordering is ignored, but partial additions/removals are detected.
   - Duplicates do matter (in quantity).

Vector Blur.description: Vector Blur applies a localized averaging effect to a given input vector. The 'Influence' parameter determines the intensity of the blur, while the 'Area' limits how many surrounding indices can affect each point. An Influence of 0 retains the original vector, whereas an Influence of 1 averages the entire vector.

Vector Chain.description: Concatenates or interleaves multiple input vectors with an offset control.

Vector Color Gradient.description: Generates R, G, B vector outputs. Features Curve control for easing and multiple interpolation modes (RGB, HSB Short, HSB Long).

Vector Distributor.description: Distributes input values into an output vector according to index positions and size.

Vector Extract.description:
Extracts values from input vector based on binary gates.
Input: Vector of floats to extract from
Idx Gates: Vector of 0s and 1s (binary mask)
Output: Vector containing input values where gate=1

Vector Feedback.description: Vector Feedback takes an input vector and applies feedback to it. The feedback is a product of the previous value and a feedback factor.

Vector File.description: Reads vector lines from a file and appends input vectors to it.

Vector Fire.description: A conditional vector routing node. It has two triggers: 'Fire' and 'vFire'. When 'Fire' is greater than 0, the entire input vector is routed to the output. 'vFire' serves as an index-wise trigger, routing values from input to output based on changes in its own indices.

Vector Fold.description: Folds a larger input vector into a smaller output vector by wrapping and summing values.

Vector Getter.description: Reads elements from an input vector at selected indices.

Vector Hold.description: Captures and holds an input vector using hold, keep and trigger controls.

Vector Insert.description: Inserts all values from Insert into Input at the zero-based Idx position. Idx is clamped between 0 and the size of Input, so 0 prepends and the input size appends.

Vector Interpolation.description: Resamples an input vector to a chosen size using interpolation.

Vector Inverter.description: Inverts specific indices of a vector based on an invert mask. For each index where invert[i] is non-zero, output[i] = 1 - input[i].

Vector Item Operations.description: Applies a selected arithmetic operation element by element to two input vectors.

Vector Matrix Offset.description: Applies spatial offset to a matrix of angle values. Input is a 1D vector representing a 2D matrix of angles (0-1). Width and Height define matrix dimensions. Offset ranges are dynamically scaled: OffsetX ranges from -width/2 to +width/2, OffsetY from -height/2 to +height/2. When Bounds=true, values wrap around; when Bounds=false, out-of-bounds values are set to zero. Output vector always maintains the same size as the matrix.

Vector Matrix Quadrants.description: Creates quadrants on a matrix. QuadrantH and QuadrantW define the size of each quadrant. QuadSel selects which quadrant is highlighted (filled with 1s). The output is a 1D vector representing the unfolded matrix.

Vector Matrix Radial Symmetry.description: Applies radial symmetry from matrix center using concentric rings. Two modes: Spatial (moves values) or Value Inversion (applies 1-x). Input is mapped row-by-row to a Columns x Rows matrix.

Vector Matrix Reflect.description: Transforms a 1D vector as a 2D matrix with rotation and reflection operations. Input vector is interpreted as a matrix with specified width and height dimensions.

Vector Matrix Resize.description: Resamples a 2D matrix (stored as a 1D vector) to a new size. Input is treated as a row-major matrix with dimensions inWidth x inHeight, and output is resized to outWidth x outHeight.

Vector Matrix Symmetry.description: Reflects input vector values in X or Y based on matrix configuration. Two modes: Spatial (moves values) or Value Inversion (applies 1-x). Input is mapped row-by-row to a Columns x Rows matrix.

Vector Modulator.description: Modulates a source vector with another vector using an amount control.

Vector Morphology.description: Analyzes vector values using an epsilon tolerance and optional circular boundaries.

Vector Morphology VV.description: Analyzes vector morphology using an epsilon tolerance and optional circular boundaries, outputting grouped values.

Vector Operations.description: Reduces a vector using minimum, maximum, sum, mean, difference, deviation or size operations.

Vector Pointer.description: The vectorPointer node takes a source vector and uses the pointer vector to find the closest values in the source. If ampTrig is true, the resulting output vector will be multiplied by the amps vector. Otherwise, it will be set to 1 for every closest value found. The output represents the 'activity' at each position of the source vector.

Vector Preset Easer.description: Smoothly transitions vector values over a configurable duration.

Vector Primitives.description: Renders configurable geometric primitives into a texture with color, size, position and rotation controls.

Vector Region.description: Outputs a sub-vector of the input vector, comprised between the indices defined by Idx Min and Idx Max

Vector Region VV.description: Outputs a vector of sub-vectors from the input vector. Each sub-vector is defined by corresponding indices in Idx Min and Idx Max vectors

Vector Reorder.description: Sorts, reverses or bypasses the input vector.

Vector Resize.description: Changes vector size by resampling or filling new elements.

Vector Rotator.description: Rotates the element positions in an input vector.

Vector Sampler.description: Samples n evenly-spaced elements from the input vector.

Vector Selector.description: Selects elements from an input vector and outputs their values and indices, optionally preserving positions.

Vector Sequencer.description: A sequencer that takes multiple input vectors and selects values based on phasor and index input. It can operate in probabilistic or deterministic mode.Outputs scalar values and vector sequences, with customizable GUI display size.

Vector Setter.description:
This node takes an input vector of floats and lets you replace specific elements at given indices, then outputs the modified vector. You choose which positions to change with the “Index” vector and what values to write with the “Set To” vector. If “Set To” has only one value, that value is used for all indices. If it has fewer values than indices, the last value is reused to fill the rest. If it has more values, the extra ones are ignored.

When “Accum” is off, each calculation starts from the current input vector. When “Accum” is on, the node starts from the previous output (as long as it’s the same size as the input), so earlier edits stay in place until you overwrite them. The “Update Mode” menu controls what triggers a recalculation: “OnIndex” reacts to index changes, “OnValue” reacts to value changes, and “Always” reacts to both, while input changes always update the result.

Vector Split.description: This module splits and resizes the input vector for it to return just the values which are between min and max

Vector Storage.description: Stores and recalls multiple vector presets, allowing real-time switching between stored states

Vector Switcher.description: Selects one of multiple vector inputs.

Vector Symmetry.description: Repeats the beginning of a vector in alternating forward and mirrored segments. Symmetry sets the number of additional segments; RepEdge repeats the endpoint at each reflection.

Vector Timer.description: Passes changed vector elements immediately, then resets each element to zero after its duration in milliseconds.

Vector To Color.description: Converts vector channel values into a color with red, green, blue and alpha outputs.

Vector of Vector Display.description:
Displays vector<vector<float>> data as multiple lines.
Supports both a floating window and an embedded node widget.

Vector to Coordinates.description:
Converts linear indices to normalized 2D coordinates (0..1).
Given W×H matrix dimensions, transforms index vector into X and Y coordinate vectors.

Vector to Texture.description: Converts vector values into a texture with configurable dimensions.

Vertical Profile Table.description: Loads a vertical profile table from a file and outputs its data.

Video Buffer.description: Stores a rolling buffer of video frames with recording, capacity and FPS controls.

Video File.description: Loads and plays a video file as Playmodes frames with scratch, rotation, flip and opacity controls.

Video Grabber.description: Captures camera video as Playmodes frames with resolution, orientation, mask and frame-wait controls.

Video Header.description: Reads a delayed frame from a video buffer using milliseconds or BPM-derived timing.

Video Player.description: Plays a video file with loop, speed and position controls and outputs its texture.

Video Player Scrub.description: Loads a video and outputs the frame at a normalized position.

Video Renderer.description: Renders a Playmodes video frame with output resolution, position and opacity controls.

Voice Expanding.description: Expands a small number of input voices (pitch + gate) over a larger vector. Pitches are duplicated to fill the output slots, and incoming gates are distributed sequentially to the corresponding pitch slots in the output.

Voice Expanding 2.description: Expands input voices sequentially over a larger vector. New values are allocated to the next available output slot. Pitch and aux values are retained after gate off.

Voice Stealing.description: Manages polyphonic voice allocation with auxiliary inputs. Assigns incoming notes and auxiliary signals to available voices.

Void Burst.description: Expands each incoming void trigger into a burst of void outputs spread across frames. Frame Gap sets how many empty frames sit between each trigger; 0 fires the whole burst in the current frame.

Void Counter.description: Counts incoming void events and outputs the count. Can be reset manually or automatically after N events.

Void Gate.description:
Passes incoming trigger events only while Gate is enabled.

**Inputs**

**[ Void In]** Trigger events to filter.

**[ Gate]** 0 blocks events; 1 passes events immediately.

**Output**

**[ Void Out]** Emits one event for each accepted input trigger.

**Notes**

Changing Gate does not emit an event or replay previously blocked triggers.

Void OR.description:
Combines several trigger inputs into one output. Every incoming event is forwarded immediately.

**Inputs**

**[ In 0]** Trigger input 0. Every event on this input fires Void Out.

**[ In 1]** Trigger input 1. Every event on this input fires Void Out.

**[ In 2]** Trigger input 2. Every event on this input fires Void Out.

**[ In 3]** Trigger input 3. Every event on this input fires Void Out.

**[ In n]** Additional trigger input created when Inputs is increased. n is the zero-based input index.

**Output**

**[ Void Out]** Combined trigger stream. Multiple inputs firing in the same frame produce multiple events; they are not deduplicated.

**Inspector**

**[ Inputs]** Number of trigger inputs. The default is four; reducing it removes inputs from the end.

Void Switch.description: Routes one of N void trigger inputs to a single void trigger output. The 'Active' parameter selects which input is live.

Void to Tick.description: Generates a scalar trigger (0 → 1 → 0) in response to a void input over consecutive frames.

Wavescope.description: Displays SuperCollider audio waveforms with freeze, trigger stabilization, gain and clipping indicators.

**Inspector: model and inference**

**[ Model path]** Path to a compiled Core ML pose model, normally inside data/yolo/models.

**[ Available models]** Model chooser listing models found in data/yolo/models.

**[ Rescan models]** Refreshes the model list after adding or removing model files.

**[ Compute (0 All 1 GPU 2 ANE 3 CPU)]** Core ML compute selection: 0 permits all units; 1 requests CPU/GPU; 2 requests CPU/Neural Engine; 3 uses CPU.

**[ Apply model / compute]** Loads the selected model and compute configuration on the next update.

**[ Frames (0 Latest 1 Drop busy)]** 0 keeps the latest pending frame; 1 rejects incoming frames while inference is busy.

**[ Person confidence]** Minimum confidence for person detection.

**[ Inference limit (0 unlimited)]** Maximum accepted inference frame rate. 0 removes the limit.

**[ Letterbox gray]** Padding brightness, from 0 to 255, used when resizing a frame to the model input.

**[ Pause inference]** Stops submitting new frames. An already running inference may still complete.

**Inspector: preview and joints**

**[ Show texture]** Shows the analyzed image behind the overlays.

**[ Mirror view]** Mirrors only the preview horizontally. Published coordinates keep the source orientation.

**[ Skeleton]** Draws bones between valid joints in the preview.

**[ Joints]** Draws markers at valid joint positions.

**[ Boxes]** Draws the detected person's bounding box.

**[ Person scores]** Shows the detected person's confidence score.

**[ Joint names]** Shows joint-name labels beside valid joint markers.

**[ Joint scores]** Shows confidence values beside valid joint markers.

**[ Joint confidence]** Minimum confidence for a joint to update its coordinate outputs and appear in overlays.

**[ Joint radius]** Joint-marker radius in source-image pixels, scaled with the preview.

**[ Line width]** Skeleton line width used by the preview.

**[ Status]** Read-only model, processing-time and frame-submission diagnostics.

**Notes**

Requires the optional ofxYOLOPose addon on Apple Silicon macOS. Coordinates use the source image with a top-left origin. Missing or low-confidence joints hold their last valid position; -1 means no valid position has been published. Invalid input, model reload, deactivation or a source-size reset can clear outputs. Preview styling does not change published coordinates.
